DESCRIPTION: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `DynamicManager.apply_diagnosis()`: the damping gate keys on `diagnosis.detector` plus optional `model_id`, but the code comment and config contract say damping is per parameter (“no param adjusted more than once per N rounds”). This causes false suppression across different parameters emitted by the same detector. Evidence: the gate compares `adj["detector"] == diagnosis.detector`, while one detector can drive multiple distinct transforms/parameters (`mu` can escalate through `widen_mu_window` and later `prefer_novelty`; `verification` can map to directive injection vs trust-flagging). Blocking by detector identity violates the declared damping scope and can suppress a needed second parameter change even when the parameter itself has not been touched.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Change damping to key on the actual parameter being changed for the selected chain step, plus model scope when applicable, instead of detector identity.

FOLLOW: This fix changes damping semantics across all chain-driven pathologies. `_record_adjustment()` already records `"parameter"`, so no schema change is required there. However, direct/special-case branches that bypass chains must no longer remain outside chain resolution, otherwise they will evade parameter-based damping again. The replacement above folds `dispatch_false_positive`, `verification_miscalibration`, and `mu_novelty_disagree` into normal chain resolution, which also aligns their behaviour with remediation-state tracking and P-pass. New downstream issue revealed: deferred remediation approval still damps by detector rather than parameter, so the same bug exists in `approve_deferred_remediation()`.

DESCRIPTION: `bench/dm/_immune.py`, `check_dispatch_health()`: dispatch false-positive detection is non-idempotent across historical blocks because `_dispatch_blocks` and `_dispatch_successes_after_block` are never pruned or acknowledged, and the uniqueness key is only `dispatch_fp_{model_id}_{block_round}`. This is a correctness-through-performance issue inside the immune boundary.
